clue.text: Wait patiently in view, drinking dry one

indicators.note: something drinking takes liquid inside it, so the view word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a sight is a view
I is the Roman numeral one
TT is teetotal, someone who is dry

explanation.surface: Someone waits in plain sight, sipping a dry drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' is the container signal; 'dry' is the crossword staple for teetotal, and 'in' after 'Wait patiently' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put without acting is to hold firm and wait patiently, an idiom.

clue.text: Criminal was almost shot-does it matter?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means one letter of the word shot is dropped, here its opening S

explanation.surface: A gangster nearly fired a gun, but shrugs it off with a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SHOT to HOT; 'Criminal' then rearranges WAS plus HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive retort asking why anyone should care, an idiom of indifference.

clue.text: Go on stage and show one's back!

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
a stage of a contest is a round

explanation.surface: A stage direction telling an actor to walk on and face away from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on stage' reads as one theatrical instruction, but splits into Go and stage, with 'on' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating to face the other way presents your rear to onlookers.

clue.text: Incensed one judge

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A single judge is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Incensed means made very angry, a synonym.

clue.text: Lively nightclub, place where trouble is likely to break out?

definitions.text: place where trouble is likely to break out?

explanation.surface: A busy club where a fight could start.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular, buzzing venue and a flashpoint of likely conflict are both described by this phrase.

clue.text: Credit is doubled for use in emergency

indicators.note: doubled says the word is appears twice in a row

explanation.surface: A credit line is doubled to cope with an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for use in' is linking material between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty, a synonym.

clue.text: Cause a noisy disturbance in lift, one in prison

parts.note: to lift is to raise

indicators.note: one in prison means the numeral sits inside the slang word for jail

parts.note: can is American slang for prison
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A prisoner kicks up a row while being taken up in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link; the second puts I inside CAN to give CAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for making a loud fuss or creating uproar, after the troublesome brother in Genesis.

clue.text: Southern sugar refiner, say

parts.note: Tate (of Tate & Lyle) was a British sugar refining company

explanation.surface: A sugar company from the South makes a statement.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate & Lyle is a long-established British sugar refiner, founder Henry Tate.
explanation.definitionFit: To say is to declare or assert, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Prevent from participating in hobby?

explanation.surface: Being kept off the team turns the sport into a mere pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: To bench a player keeps them out of play; a secondary activity or pastime is another sense.

clue.text: Bond Street catching right storm

indicators.note: catching means the street word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a way is a street, as in Milky Way or a road name
to rant is to storm, rage loudly

explanation.surface: Bond Street, the London shopping street, gets caught in a heavy downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond Street is a smart London shopping street, so the surface reads as one name; 'Bond' alone is the definition, and 'catching' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a binding promise or guarantee, as a written assurance on goods is.

clue.text: Expert is reportedly put in charge

indicators.note: put in signals the sounded piece sits inside the word for charge

parts.note: a ward is a charge, someone in another's care

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is is rendered as it is spoken, with a buzzing Z

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like IZ

explanation.surface: Word is that a specialist has been appointed to run things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives the spoken form of 'is', with its buzzing Z sound; 'put in' is the container signal, and 'charge' means a person in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A whizz or ace at something is called this, an informal synonym for a skilled person.

clue.text: British goal got from a corner

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A British football goal scored from a corner kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corner' looks like football's corner kick but is the definition, a turn in a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve or turn in a road is a corner.

clue.text: A European king must go to give assent

indicators.note: must go says the letter for king is taken out of the European word

parts.note: a Greek is a European
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: A European monarch is forced to abdicate before he will consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must go' is the deletion signal; 'to' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur or consent is to give assent, a synonym.

clue.text: Gradually sample tea maybe

parts.note: a piece is a sample or portion of something
tea is an example of a meal, the evening one in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone tastes tea slowly, sip by sip.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, tea can mean an early evening meal as well as the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Done bit by bit, little by little, is a synonym for gradually.

clue.text: Steal a march on unfashionable comic

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a wit is a comic person, a joker

explanation.surface: A dated comedian is outmanoeuvred.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone by being cleverer is to gain an advantage over them.

clue.text: A western with a pretty awful lawman and gunfighter

indicators.note: awful suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cowboy film featuring a rather terrible sheriff and gunslinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the fodder pieces and gives no letters; 'awful' rearranges A, W and A PRETTY.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous US marshal of the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral was both lawman and gunfighter.

clue.text: Notice old man in study, poker-faced

indicators.note: in places the notice and old man pieces inside the word for study

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room
an ad is a notice, an advertisement
pa is a father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Dad sits in the study reading a notice without expression.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressionless face showing no emotion, as a card player keeps, is a synonym.

clue.text: Messenger-boy committing crime in church house

indicators.note: committing is read as taking in, so the boy's word holds the crime inside

parts.note: a page is a boy who carries messages
arson is a crime, setting fire deliberately

explanation.surface: An errand boy sets fire to the vicar's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'committing' is the container signal: to commit is to consign into custody, so the boy takes the crime inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: The residence provided for a parish minister by the church is a synonym.

clue.text: Our spice abroad is dear

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Our imported spice is expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' suggests costly, as the surface wants, but means beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured and beloved is described this way, a synonym.

clue.text: Artist, one arriving in time for broadcast

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: arriving in means the numeral enters the word for time

parts.note: a date is a time
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter turns up on time for a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to send out or spread in all directions, a synonym for broadcast.

clue.text: Some ordered a mild cheese

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some customers asked for a mild cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coat is one variety.

clue.text: False rumour in article penned by comic

indicators.note: penned by means the article is enclosed within the comic word

parts.note: a card is a comic, an amusing person
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A comedian writes a fake story into an article.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded report or hoax, a synonym.

clue.text: Touch of candour to guarantee criticism

indicators.note: touch of means a small amount, the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: to ensure is to guarantee

explanation.surface: A little honesty ensures criticism will follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal disapproval or strong criticism is a synonym.

clue.text: Beer stocked by the German merchant

indicators.note: stocked by means the beer is held inside the German article

parts.note: der is the German for the (masculine)
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A German trader keeps beer in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who buys and sells goods is a synonym.

clue.text: Force prisoners on to coach

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: Inmates are made to board a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a bus, but is the verb, to train.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel or restrict is a synonym for force.

clue.text: Lowest point in drain in need of repair

indicators.note: in need of repair suggests broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken drain is the lowest point.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the bottom or lowest point, a synonym.

clue.text: Initially propose to girl in writing

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man begins to propose to a girl in a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary written language without metre is a kind of writing.

clue.text: The fire-raiser's game?

explanation.surface: An arsonist's favourite pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal rod raises a fire when stirred in the hearth, and a card game is the other sense.

clue.text: Severe test of French in exam

indicators.note: in places the French word inside the exam word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A French exam is a gruelling experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful or trying experience is a synonym for a severe test.

clue.text: Refuse what may come after chain letters that are unsolicited?

parts.note: junk is refuse, rubbish
chain mail is armour, so mail can follow chain

explanation.surface: Discarding chain letters, which arrive uninvited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the verb, but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted advertising post is this, letters nobody asked for.

clue.text: Band in street, all set

parts.note: ripe means ready, all set

explanation.surface: A band is in the street, all ready to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow strip or band of colour is a synonym.

clue.text: Try to catch words of approval

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
to catch words is to hear them

explanation.surface: Straining to catch the cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of agreement in Parliament, repeating a word, expresses approval.
